mainCommitMeaning: main was pushed to the release commit before the tag was pushed, so the release was cut on an already published branch commit
note: The pinned artifact was built from fd63317 (the source commit that carries the cold-archive identity changes). a433b6e is the release commit: it only adds the pinned tarball, release/manifest.json, release/SHA256SUMS and the rewritten host acceptance evidence, and it changes no file inside the package allow-list. Nothing was rebuilt for the tag.

node22.note: the official darwin-arm64 binary downloaded from nodejs.org, run on a copy of the release tree

noLatestRelease.meaning: every published release is a pre-release, so the repository has no latest release and an RC cannot be mistaken for a stable channel

postPublishHostAcceptance.installedTarball: the tarball anonymously downloaded from the public release URL, not the local release/ copy

verificationLimits: The acceptance harness ran on macOS arm64 with Node v26.12.0; the CI run covers the same content on ubuntu-latest with Node 22.19.0 and 24.x.
CI host acceptance repacks with Node 22 npm, so its bytes differ from the pinned ones; only the content digest is compared there, as documented in RELEASE.md section 1.
Only 0.2.1-rc.2 was re-accepted against the anonymously downloaded bytes; the other two hosts were accepted locally against the pinned tarball and in CI against the same content.

The Node 22.19.0 and 24.9.0 unit runs were executed on a copy of the release tree with the repository node_modules symlinked; they are not a full npm ci in a clean checkout (CI performs that on both versions).
remainingRisksAndUnverified: The A–E equivalence argument for the identity path rests on exhaustive differential runs plus the frozen rc.10 baseline, not on a formal proof of the regex engine: RELEASE.md risk list and docs/performance/knowledge-identity-normalization.md section 7 state that rewriting, moving or reinterpreting those collapses requires re-running the comparison.

The identity literal in identitySerialization() hard-codes six dimension names. A seventh dimension, a rename, or a dimension name added to VOLATILE_KEYS fails the property test before any pinned value is consulted, but a change that alters a value of an existing dimension is caught only by the frozen-baseline differentials.
The event-bridge tail repair is a check-then-act over a file no writer locks: an append landing between the final read and the rename can still be dropped (RELEASE.md risk 14).

satisfiesRange() compares pre-release identifiers with localeCompare, so a multi-digit pre-release ordinal orders wrongly. Not fixed; the verified host combinations do not exercise it (RELEASE.md risk 15).
